title: Cost-Benefit Analysis and Proportionality
summary: Practical techniques for assessing the costs and benefits of proposed rules, testing proportionality across firms of different sizes, and anticipating unintended consequences before rules are finalised.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Practical techniques for assessing the costs and benefits of proposed rules, testing proportionality across firms of different sizes, and anticipating unintended consequences before rules are finalised.
Learning Objectives: Apply cost-benefit techniques to a proposed rule
Assess proportionality and distributional effects across firm sizes
Identify unintended consequences and market reactions in advance
Syllabus: Impact assessment frameworks and data sources
Quantifying compliance costs and valuing hard-to-measure benefits
Proportionality: is the intervention justified by the risk?
Case study: a rule with significant unintended consequences
Intended Audience: Policy and rule-making staff developing rules, guidance and policy positions
Legal advisers and drafters working on secondary rules and supervisory guidance
Supervisors and economists who contribute evidence, impact analysis or consultation input
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of policy, legal or supervisory work is helpful. No formal legal or economics training is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Regulatory Policy and Governance (2012)
OECD, Best Practice Principles for Regulatory Policy: Regulatory Impact Assessment (2020)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
